subject: physics
question_text: Obtain an equation for the frequency of oscillation of a spring of force constant k to which a mass m is attached.

verification.note: The mark split is invented and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The question itself is sourced, not invented. AI physics check 2026-08-24: formulas, signs, numbers and claims verified against NCERT Class-11 conventions; corrections applied to explanation text (why / common_mistakes / memory_tip), marked answer lines unchanged unless factually wrong.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The arrangement
steps.why: The figure fixes the mean position O, where the hanging mass rests: the spring is already stretched by mg/k and its pull balances the weight. Every y in the answer is measured from O, not from the natural length.
common_mistakes: Measuring y from the natural length of the spring instead of from the mean position O.

recall.must_convey: That a spring hangs from a support with a mass m attached, pulled down through y from the mean position O.
accept: draw the spring with the mass
mark the mean position and y

steps.memory_tip: Draw the hanging spring with the mean position O marked — every y is measured from O.

steps.label: The force law
lines: Pull the mass down through a distance y and
release it. The spring pulls it back with a
The minus sign shows F and y point opposite
ways. By Newton’s second law F = m a, so
a ∝ −y, which IS simple harmonic motion.
steps.why: Showing a ∝ −y first is what earns the right to use the SHM formulas at all; quoting T = 2π√(m/k) without it assumes the answer. Here F = −ky is the NET force measured from O — the extra spring pull beyond the part that balances mg. Gravity cancels, so the vertical spring obeys the same equation as a horizontal one.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus sign, which turns an oscillation into a runaway.

recall.must_convey: That F is minus k y, so m a is minus k y and a is minus k by m times y, proving SHM.
accept: a equals minus k by m into y
a is proportional to minus y
reject: draw the spring with the mass

steps.memory_tip: Show F = −ky gives a = −(k/m)y FIRST; that line earns the right to use the SHM formulas.

steps.label: The frequency
steps.why: A stiffer spring (larger k) or a lighter mass both raise the frequency — which is exactly what the square root says.
common_mistakes: Writing n = 2π√(k/m), forgetting that n is the reciprocal of T.

recall.must_convey: That omega is root k by m, T is 2 pi root m by k, and n is one by 2 pi times root k by m.
accept: omega is root k by m
T is 2 pi root m by k
n is one by two pi root k by m

steps.memory_tip: ω² = k/m, so n = (1/2π)√(k/m). Stiffer spring or lighter mass → higher frequency.
